messages:
lex: quick RFC follow-up — the device dispatch refactor we merged last week is behaving oddly on L4. probing moved into the main attach path and we gate kernel choices by reported SM features. seeing higher p50 on certain attention workloads when tile_size=64. anyone else hit this?

mai: saw a spike in the telemetry stream yes. L4 tends to choose the split-attn kernel because our bitmask check isn’t matching the quasi-features L4 reports. seems like a brittle equality check. :confused:

sanjay: can you paste the probe payload from one of the failing nodes?

lex: pasted a minimal example from the job that regressed:
```
SM_CAPS: 0x12
PROBE_LATENCY_MS: 0.82
AVAILABLE_KERNELS: [attention_fused, attention_split]
SELECTED: attention_split
```

mai: that 0x12 on L4 maps to {warp_shuffle, small_warp_math}. our runtime treated any small-warp flags as 'not-large-kv' which forces split. L4 actually benefits from a different fused kernel variant for short sequences.

ev an: proposal: move from exact bitmask rules to a lightweight scoring function. compute a kernel_score = sum(weight_i * feature_i) and pick the best kernel. This decouples us from weird vendor bit encodings.

lauren: scoring + metrics. we should emit a `kernel_probe.v1` event with fields: device_id, scores, selected_kernel, probe_latency_ms, model_family so we can roll back or tune weights. also flag dedicated nodes for manual review.

lex: agreed. initial patch sketch:
```
features = probe(device)
for k in kernels:
  scores[k] = dot(weights[k], features)
selected = argmax(scores)
emit_event('kernel_probe.v1', {device, scores, selected})
```
cache selected per-device / per-device-config.

sanjay: important: do NOT run scoring on every request. do it once on attach and cache. add a reprobe interval (eg. 6h) or on firmware change. we should also include a simple fast-fallback path in the runtime if selected kernel crashes or returns invalid outputs.

mai: caching + periodic re-probe seems right. for Dedicated nodes we should expose `runtime.probe.reprobe_interval` (default 21600). and add a toggle `runtime.probe.mode = [conservative|scored|optimistic]` so customers can opt-in.

evan: also consider optimistic-dispatch hybrid: assume best kernel for latency-critical traffic, but keep a fast-path to fall back to a safe kernel when a kernel error or QoS regression is detected. That avoids probe overhead on hot paths while keeping safety.

lex: good call. plan: implement scoring + per-device cache + optimistic dispatch with fast fallback. add telemetry buckets for canary vs prod. I'll open a follow-up RFC with perf targets and the telemetry schema.

lauren: assigning lex/mai/sanjay to implement and own rollout. I'll schedule a 20m sync tomorrow to align canary targets and rollback thresholds. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy pipeline started for patch `device-dispatcher-hybrid-probe` on branch main — build 4821.

infra-bot: canary rollout update — build 4821 rolled to canary-2 (h100, a100).

lex: note — L4 canary nodes not included in canary-2, will add L4 in canary-3 after we have scoring weights tuned.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded on canary-2 — build 4821.

mai: after canary-2 results look stable, I'll run a small L4 private canary with tuned weights and telemetry knobs.

evan: one more item — add unit test harness for `probe -> score -> select` with synthetic SM feature vectors so we don't regress the selection logic in future refactors.

lex: will add tests + integration test that compares selected kernel vs golden trace for sample models. thanks all.
